nodes.name: Form Trigger
nodes.notes: Standalone test harness (ADR-020) ONLY: paste a task id; Get Task fetches ALL attachments and feeds them unfiltered to the reader. Classification (which attachments are text-family) is the input-router's job (Block 4, spec 2.3), NOT the reader's - so in standalone testing attach only text files.

parameters.formDescription: Enter a ClickUp task id to extract its attachments as text.

nodes.name: When Called
nodes.notes: Production entry (called by input-router, Block 4). In: { clickup_task_id, attachments:[{att_id,title,url,ext,mime,order}] } - a PRE-CLASSIFIED, ordered text-family list (router owns the MIME/ext switch + global order, spec 2.3). Out: { blocks, clickup_task_id, warnings }. PURE function: no side-effects - the router fires `warnings` via Post Alert (single alerting choke-point).

nodes.name: Get Task
nodes.notes: TEST-HARNESS BRANCH ONLY (Form path). Authoritative attachment list via HTTP (ADR-019; the n8n ClickUp 'get' node omits attachments[]). The production When Called path skips this - the router already fetched + classified.

nodes.name: Explode Attachments
nodes.notes: Pure NORMALIZER (no classification): explode the attachments array into one item per attachment, normalizing both shapes - router-shaped {att_id,url,ext,mime,order} and raw ClickUp {id,url_w_query,extension,mimetype}. Preserves the router's order; falls back to index for the test path.

nodes.name: Fetch Attachment Binary
nodes.notes: Download bytes to a binary property (kept separate from JSON - no base64 in the flow). ClickUp url_w_query is pre-signed, so no auth header. continueRegularOutput: a fetch failure stays inline (no binary) so Docling/Build Block degrade it to [BRAK] + warning.

nodes.name: Docling Convert
nodes.notes: POST /v1/convert/file (multipart field 'files'). image_export_mode=placeholder is CRITICAL (default 'embedded' inlines base64 and explodes token cost - ADR-036 Block 1). Note: a corrupt file returns HTTP 200 with status=failure + md_content=null, so Build Block checks md_content, not the HTTP code. continueRegularOutput keeps real HTTP errors inline -> [BRAK].

nodes.name: Build Block
nodes.notes: Per-item: success -> { type:text, order, md }; any failure (fetch error, Docling error, or 200/status=failure/empty md) -> [BRAK: extraction_failed <file>] + needs_alert. Flags has_embedded on placeholder markers. Tags drive the `warnings` list Aggregate hands to the router.

nodes.name: Aggregate Blocks
nodes.notes: SOLE TERMINAL (single linear input from Build Block -> runs once over all items). Returns { blocks (sorted by order), clickup_task_id, warnings:[{source,title,err}] }. The router (Block 4) fires `warnings` via Post Alert (v1): multimodal/extraction-failed for [BRAK] files, multimodal/embedded-image-skipped for dropped in-doc images. Branch-free reader => n8n returns THIS node deterministically.
